answer: Eccentricity-gated neighbor scoring. Each agent scores peers by how far their transaction neighbors sit from the local cluster centroid; low-eccentricity agents in a hollow neighborhood get down-weighted, since honest agents occupy a dense mesa of shared counterparties. A new identity must first sustain diverse, high-eccentricity links across a broad meadow of existing clusters, which requires real counterparties and repeated interaction. An attacker therefore pays the full cost of maintaining many distinct, active neighbor sets per identity, not a one-time fee.
